title: Neumann–Lara conjecture
formal: For every finite oriented graph D whose underlying undirected graph is planar, is there a coloring \(c:V(D)\to \{0,1\}\) such that neither color class induces a directed cycle?
definitions: An oriented graph has no loops or parallel arcs and contains at most one of \((u,v)\) and \((v,u)\) for each unordered pair of distinct vertices. Its underlying simple undirected graph joins u,v exactly when one of these arcs is present. Planarity means that graph admits a drawing in the plane with edges intersecting only at common endpoints. For a vertex set X, the induced subdigraph \(D[X]\) retains every arc of D whose two endpoints lie in X. A directed cycle is a cyclic sequence of distinct vertices with all successive arcs oriented forward. A digraph is acyclic if it has no directed cycle. Color classes may be empty. This is not proper coloring: an arc may have endpoints of the same color provided no monochromatic directed cycle results. The assertion asks only for existence, without an algorithmic running-time bound.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether two acyclic classes always suffice to organize the vertices of an oriented planar graph.

importance.reason: A central directed planar-coloring conjecture linking planarity and decomposition into acyclic subgraphs.

progress.text: Li and Mohar prove two-colorability when the planar digraph has digirth at least four.
Cambie and coauthors explicitly state the general Neumann–Lara conjecture as open in Conjecture 3.

context_blocks.text: Acyclic vertex coloring permits edges within each class but forbids a cyclic chain of directed dependencies. It is therefore different from ordinary proper coloring of the underlying planar graph.
Li and Mohar settle the case without directed triangles. The unrestricted target includes directed triangles and asks whether the entire graph can still be split into only two acyclic induced parts.

The 2026 partition paper connects this conjecture to planar Hamiltonicity and induced-forest questions. Its formulation on planar triangulations has the same general coloring target, because additional oriented edges can only impose more restrictions and every oriented planar graph extends to an oriented planar triangulation after harmless small cases.

sentences: The conjecture asks whether every oriented planar graph has a two-coloring with no monochromatic directed cycle.
Arcs within a color class are allowed, so the coloring need not be proper.
Loops and opposite pairs of arcs are excluded.
The case without directed triangles is known, but directed triangles are allowed in the general target.
The question is a directed analogue of central planar graph-decomposition principles.
